Set notebook options

Load dependencies

Dataset

The dataset is for patients part of the Mt. Sinai Millions (MSM) cohort, for each patient we have some demographic information and their “medical history”. The medical history is the list of ICD codes (specifiyng diagnoses) assigned to a patient by a doctor during a hospital visit for all recorded vists for that patient. So for every visit recorded we have the set of ICD codes assigned. We will turn this long-form medical history into a set of descriptive features for each patient that are better suited to linear modelling where patients are independent data points. We also use the medical history to define the outcome we are studying for each patient and whether they experience SI, Broad SA or Narrow SA.

Plot Patient Demographics

Load clean demographics data

Code 
# all_combined_data <- load_all_combined_data(force_redo=FALSE)
demographics_df <- 
    clean_demographics_data() %>% 
    # turn columns into neat factors, leaving NAs as NAs
    factorize_demographics_data() %>% 
    # remove all patients without complete demographic records
    filter(if_all(everything(), ~!is.na(.x))) %>%
    select(
        FID,
        current_age,
        gender,
        ethnicity,
        is_deceased,
        is_religious,
        is_cisgender,
        is_married
    )

Plot individual distributions for all 40280 patients with no missing data.

Code 
make_single_ggbar <- function(col_name, plot_df=demographics_df){
    plot.obj <- 
        plot_df %>% 
        select(!!sym(col_name)) %>%
        count(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
        add_column(feature=col_name) %>%  # dummy x-axis
        mutate(pct=prop.table(n)) %>%  # counts to percentages
        arrange(!!sym(col_name)) %>% 
        mutate(ypos=1 - (cumsum(pct) - pct/2)) %>%  # percentage label position on figure
        {
            ggplot(
                data=.,
                aes(
                    x=feature,
                    y=pct,
                    fill=.data[[col_name]],
                )
            ) + 
            geom_col(position='stack') +  # stacked bar plot
            geom_text(
                aes(
                    label=scales::percent(pct, accuracy=0.1),
                    y=ypos
                ),
                vjust=0.5,    # nudge above top of bar
                size = 3
            ) + 
            scale_y_continuous(labels=scales::percent) +
            guides(fill=guide_legend(ncol=1)) +
            theme_minimal() +
            theme(
                # axis.text.x=element_text(angle=55, vjust=1, hjust=1),
                # axis.text.x = element_blank(),
                legend.position='right',
                axis.title = element_blank()
            )
        }
}
current_age_dist <- 
    demographics_df %>% select(current_age) %>% add_column(feature='age') %>%
    {
        ggplot(
            aes(x=current_age),
            data=.
        ) + 
        geom_histogram(binwidth=1) +
        # coord_flip() +
        scale_y_continuous(labels=label_number(scale_cut=cut_short_scale())) +
        theme_minimal() +
        theme(
            axis.text.x=element_text(angle=55),
            axis.title.y=element_blank()
        )
    }
# make plot with patchwork
design <- "
CCAB
DEFG
"
{
    make_single_ggbar('gender')       +
    make_single_ggbar('ethnicity')    + 
    current_age_dist +
    make_single_ggbar('is_deceased')  +
    make_single_ggbar('is_religious') +
    make_single_ggbar('is_cisgender') +
    make_single_ggbar('is_married')   +
    plot_layout(design=design)
}

Defining patient outcomes

For every patinent we want to create a discrete output column that specifies what experience (if any) the patient had with Suicidal Ideation or Actions. We have 3 lists of ICD codes, where if a patient has been assigned a code, they have the outcome for Ideation (SI), Broad Action (Broad SA) and Narrow Action (Narrow SA), and “control” if they dont match any codes across all lists.
Using these lists of codes Using the assigned ICD codes we can define these discrete columns in several other ways as follows and test for differences in model construction.

  • Full: {“None”, “SI”, “Broad SA”, “Narrow SA”}
  • SI Only: {“None”, “SI”}
  • Any SI: {“None”, “SI”, “Broad SA”, “Narrow SA”}
  • Any SA: {“None”, “Broad SA”, “Narrow SA”}

Note that all encodings use the same set of samples, just changing the case/control labels. We can also assign other phenotypes, such as Alcohol Use Disorder and Substance Use Disorder from the ICD codes in the same way.
